channel.title: Arabian Grid — MEA Renewable Energy Intelligence
channel.description: Decision-grade market intelligence on renewable energy, solar, BESS, and green hydrogen across the Middle East and Africa. Curated by Krishna Singh, Chief Business Officer.

item.title: Angola: The Renewable Energy Market Most People Are Sleeping On
item.description: A 16-page executive study distilled into 8 slides. Covers resource potential, Angola Energia 2025 targets, the 600 MW green hydrogen export project, Law 6/25 regulatory opening, and the $23 billion investment gap.

item.title: Algeria: RE Capacity, FIT Corrections, and the Hydrogen Infrastructure Play
item.description: Installed renewable capacity at end-2025 is 446 MW — not 880 MW as commonly cited. 2.6 GW under construction, 1.48 GW commissioning by August 2026. FIT rates corrected: solar PV at 15.94 DZD/kWh (1–5 MW). Hydrogen targets ~40 TWh/year by 2040.

item.title: The BESS Surge: Why 2026 Is the Inflection Year for Battery Storage in the Gulf
item.description: EWEC's 1.5 GW Al Ajban tender, Masdar's 5 GW pipeline, and the regulatory shifts that are turning BESS from a backup plan into a primary revenue stream. Brief in progress.

item.title: Qatar: EPC-Only Solar and the Kahramaa Licensing Gate
item.description: Qatar's utility-scale solar uses the EPC model — not IPP. Samsung C&T has won every major contract. Kahramaa Grade A licensing is the gate. What foreign EPCs actually need to know about market entry. Brief in progress.

item.title: Saudi Arabia's Hydrogen Corridor: NEOM, SPARK, and the $5B Question
item.description: NEOM's 2.2 GW electrolyser, ACWA Power's ammonia offtake strategy, and the regulatory vacuum that still defines Saudi green hydrogen project finance. Brief in progress.

item.title: Bahrain Steel 110 MWp: What a Landmark Deal Teaches About C&I Solar in the Gulf
item.description: Ground-mounted and rooftop hybrid, long-term O&M, and the offtaker negotiation dynamics that made this one of the most significant C&I solar contracts in Bahrain's history. Brief in progress.
